newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to take hard line against boat people.
newsitem.headline: Australia to take hard line against boat people.

text.p: The Australian government on Sunday announced a tougher line against boat people trying to jump its immigration queues after it blocked an apparently organised attempt to slip 139 people into the country.
"We are not standing for this nonsense," Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on televison as the latest group of Asian boat people were taken to a detention centre.

"People ought to be aware of that and let that message ripple up the bamboo grapevine so that people can desist from this dangerous and foolhardly queue-jumping," he said, adding that the origin of the latest attempt was being investigated.
Each year several hundred illegal immigrants arrive on the Australian coast or one of its islands. Almost all are sent home after apprehension.
"We are going to be a whole lot more rigorous and maintain that degree of rigour with regard to protecting our borders and maintaining our sovereignty," Fischer said.
The latest arrivals, originally estimated by officials to number 138, were detected off the northeast tip of Australia last week when their large steel trawler was stranded on a sandbank.
A customs boat took them to a nearby island where some escaped.
A spokeswoman told Reuters that the Immigration Department now believed all had been captured, including one who jumped off the boat and swam to a nearby island.
All but two were now at the remote Port Hedland detention centre on Australia's northwest coast, where boat people usually arrive, typically in small overcrowded ships.
Asked whether the latest boat was part of an organised racket, Fischer said: "I happen to notice (their) designer T-shirts, the sunglasses, the suits.
"Clearly this particular operation involved a level of sophistication which is a concern."
Australia already had 182 boat people in detention when the latest group arrived.
Most boat people come to Australia from Asia, although some have come from as far away as Romania and Poland.
